intro: Match each moment to the principle on your card.

left.label: Colonists say only their own elected assemblies can tax them (1765)
The Declaration says government gets its power from the consent of the governed (1776)
Madison says each branch needs the power to resist the others (1788)
The Bill of Rights protects speech, press and religion (1791)
McCulloch v. Maryland: a state can't tax the national bank (1819)
Congress uses the necessary and proper clause to charter a bank the Constitution never names (1816)

rationale.a: The card: the people elect officials to make decisions for them.
rationale.b: The card: government's power comes from the people, and it rules only with their agreement.
rationale.c: Federalist 51. The card: each branch can block or limit the others.
rationale.d: The First Amendment. The card: freedoms government can't take away.
rationale.e: The card: when the nation and a state clash, valid federal law wins.
rationale.f: The card: government can only do what the Constitution allows. Opponents said Congress had gone too far.

a: Who do the colonists say gets to tax them?
Look for the principle about electing officials.
b: Where does the power come from?
Consent of the governed sits inside one principle.
c: Branches resisting each other means what?
e: It's a state against the nation.
Look for the principle about levels of government.
f: Opponents said Congress went beyond the Constitution.
Look for the principle about going too far.
